lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: Forging adversarial images
unit.description: Builds adversarial examples by optimizing input pixels against a fixed pretrained classifier, then adds perceptual constraints and reviews physical-world adversarial patches.
unit.summary: A pretrained ImageNet classifier can be attacked by treating the input image itself as the optimization variable while keeping model weights fixed [ts=653s]. The first objective finds an image whose prediction is close to the iguana label, but because the input space is enormous, the result is unlikely to look like a real iguana to humans [ts=920s]. A stronger attack starts from or stays close to a real cat image while still pushing the model toward the iguana label, making the result visually plausible but misclassified [ts=1082s]. The segment then grounds the idea in physical examples, including images that change phone-model predictions and adversarial patches that can hide a person from a detector [ts=1195s]. The instructor highlights that patch objectives can include practical terms such as printable colors and smoothness, and that attacks can transfer in black-box settings when models learn similar salient features [ts=1322s].

key_points.text: Adversarial image generation can minimize distance between the model prediction and a target label while treating pixels as trainable variables.
The model weights remain fixed; gradients are taken with respect to input pixels rather than parameters.
Most optimized target-class images may fall outside the real-image manifold because the input space is much larger than the space of natural images.
A perceptual regularization term can keep the forged image close to a chosen cat image while changing the target prediction.
Physical adversarial patches can be optimized against detector outputs and then printed, with loss terms that enforce printability and smoothness.

kp_catalog.name: Input-space optimization for adversarial examples
kp_catalog.description: Constructing adversarial examples by holding model parameters fixed and optimizing the input pixels to make a chosen target label likely.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: This is the first concrete attack construction and relies directly on loss design and gradients with respect to inputs [ts=653s][ts=718s].

kp_catalog.name: Perceptual constraints for adversarial examples
kp_catalog.description: Adding a closeness constraint or regularizer so the optimized image remains near a human-recognizable source image while the model predicts a target class.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor modifies the attack objective so the adversarial image stays close to a cat image while being classified as iguana [ts=1082s].

kp_catalog.name: Physical adversarial patches and transferability
kp_catalog.description: Adversarial patterns can be optimized, printed, and applied in the physical world, and may transfer across models with similar learned features.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The physical patch examples demonstrate practical attack construction, printability constraints, and black-box transfer intuition [ts=1243s][ts=1322s][ts=1382s].
